title: Lesion atlas: septal and atrioventricular lesions (AVSD, common valve, straddling, VSD)

items.question: An atrioventricular junction lesion is found with no other defect. Which association should be considered?
options: No association; isolated lesions are always sporadic
items.explanation: Isolated AV junction lesions are often associated with aneuploidy, including trisomy 21.

items.question: Which view best shows atrioventricular valve morphology, chordae and papillary muscles in short axis?
options: A sagittal view of the fetal thorax
items.explanation: A sagittal view of the thorax best shows the valve in short axis.

items.question: Peak inflow velocity across a stenotic atrioventricular valve looks modest. Why be careful?
options: Peak velocity may underestimate stenosis because fetal flow can redistribute
Velocity cannot be measured in the fetus
There is no reason; modest velocity excludes stenosis
items.explanation: Fetal flow redistribution means peak velocity may underestimate severity.

items.question: AVSD is suspected. What should be examined en face?
options: The left atrioventricular valve, for a cleft or common orifice
The pulmonary valve, for leaflet number
items.explanation: The left AV valve should be examined en face for a cleft or common orifice.

items.question: In AVSD, what does a smaller right-to-left ventricular inflow angle indicate?
items.explanation: The inflow angle is measured from an apical four-chamber view; a smaller angle indicates greater imbalance.

items.question: Features of an unbalanced AVSD are seen. Which condition should be considered?
items.explanation: With unbalanced AVSD, right or left atrial isomerism should be considered.

items.question: A common atrioventricular valve is seen. Which venous anomalies often accompany it?
options: Bilateral superior venae cavae, interrupted inferior vena cava, total anomalous pulmonary venous return
Agenesis of the ductus venosus only
items.explanation: These three are listed with a common AV valve.

items.question: With a common atrioventricular valve, what may be missed unless specifically looked for?
items.explanation: Additional VSDs may be missed unless looked for.

items.question: Chordae from one atrioventricular valve pass through a VSD and attach in the opposite ventricle. What is this called, and why does it matter?
options: A straddling valve; closure of the VSD may be impossible
An overriding valve; it has no surgical relevance
A cleft valve; it always closes after birth
items.explanation: This is straddling. A straddling or overriding valve may make VSD closure impossible and require a single-ventricle approach.

items.question: Straddling valve with a hypoplastic left atrioventricular valve. Which risk follows?
items.explanation: With a hypoplastic left AV valve, the fetus is at risk of left atrial hypertension.

items.question: How is straddling anatomy best shown?
options: Video clips and live scanning, from several views
One still image in the four-chamber view
It cannot be shown before birth
items.explanation: Clips and live scanning show straddling better than stills; combined 2D, colour and pulsed-wave from multiple views are recommended.
